calls.reason: Ars and GitHub document cost-driven billing changes, but ITPro's spending controls do not show that well-funded enterprises rejected useful AI purchases because prices became unjustifiable.
OpenAI's preview card reports lower hallucination rates on tests but contrary anecdotal feedback. Its self-correction description does not establish that faulty checking causes more hallucinations.

OpenAI reports reasoning gains and ARC Prize finds improved adaptation, but neither clearly establishes materially new useful tasks beyond accuracy improvements. The packet also lacks broad evidence of a plateau.

The Decoder supports substantial losses at both firms and reports Anthropic's $2.7 billion loss outlook. It does not establish that both companies designed pricing to acquire customers rather than earn profit.
Microsoft's disclosure describes continued AI capacity expansion. The packet establishes no substantial AI withdrawal whose stock and reputational consequences could test the prediction.

Andersen remains in discovery in the supplied records. The Anthropic settlement rejects model deletion, but does not establish the training-liability victory needed to test the predicted retraining consequences.
